39.text: The reindeer begins to shed its hair in the spring, and finishes in the

40.text: middle of summer. Well-fed animals start shedding before lean ones, and

41.text: grown animals before younger ones. A herd in good condition will finish

42.text: two weeks earlier than a lean one. The new hair is short and sleek, but it

43.text: thickens rapidly; and in September the skins of fawns are suitable for making

44.text: winter garments. For this purpose skins of fawns are used almost exclusively.

45.text: The fawns are killed at two set periods in early fall, according to the kind

46.text: of fur desired. The late fall fawn-skins are used only for heavy overcoats;

47.text: and the skins of grown animals, for sleeping-room coverings, bedding, and the

48.text: like. For the Russian trade, spring fawn-skins of smaller size, called by the

49.text: traders “vyporotki” (выпоротки), are required. Of these, the black skins are

50.text: more highly valued, and bring almost three times the price of gray ones.
